What is Feature Scaling?
Bringing every feature onto a common numeric scale

Feature Scaling in Machine Learning
Slide 2 / 12


Definition
Feature Scaling is a preprocessing step that transforms numeric features so they share a similar range — preventing large-value features from dominating the learning process.

04
When is Feature Scaling Used?
Distance-based and gradient-based algorithms need it most

Feature Scaling in Machine Learning
Slide 4 / 12
Algorithms That REQUIRE Scaling


K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN)
Distance-based similarity


Support Vector Machine (SVM)
Margin optimization


Logistic Regression
Gradient descent


Neural Networks
Stable weight updates


K-Means Clustering
Centroid distance
Algorithms That DON'T Require Scaling










Decision Trees & Random Forests


Why not?
Tree-based models split features by threshold, not distance. The absolute magnitude of each feature has no impact on the decision boundary.

FORMULA

10
Limitations of Feature Scaling
Know when it helps and when it hurts

Feature Scaling in Machine Learning
Slide 10 / 12



Not Needed for Trees
Decision Trees and Random Forests split by thresholds, so scaling has no effect on their performance.



Outlier Sensitivity
Min-Max Scaling can be distorted by a single outlier, compressing all other values into a tiny range.



Extra Preprocessing
Scaling adds a step to the pipeline; parameters must be fit on training and applied to test data consistently.



Wrong Method Hurts
Choosing the wrong scaling method for the data distribution can actually reduce model performance.
